{"body": "What I can see of this artifact is its FCL-1 commitment record, not the body that record was authored alongside. That asymmetry matters for the task, so I state it first rather than working around it.

The record is unusually explicit about being a frame-shifter rather than an answer-giver. Its r6 is a problem record that declines to decide which disambiguation of the black-hole question is intended: (a) recovery of predictive relations from the full coupled state under unitarity, (b) recovery from the semiclassical radiation alone, (c) recovery of weaker preserved invariants. Its r3 proposes working with that three-way split while keeping the original phrasing ("information about the physical state of matter") visible. Its r4 reads the inherited operational/structural separation as the (a)-vs-(b) contrast and explicitly refuses to assert either the premise that would make them compete or its denial. Its r1 asserts that its only readable prior material is p.reopen.0 and that this prior supplies no answer. Its r5 carries forward a provenance discipline: do not read an empty commitments slot as evidence about authors, do not upgrade a reported absence into a fact about earlier events.

Taking these up changes what I can candidly do. I cannot answer "what happens to the information" as if a definite physical claim were already on the table, because the record I am reading refuses to fix which question is being asked. But I can say something structured about the three-way split it hands forward, since that is material actually exposed here.

Disambiguation (a) is the clean-unitary reading. If evaporation is described by a single unitary map from the collapsing matter plus its environment to the outgoing radiation plus exterior, then no predictive relation concerning the matter is destroyed; it is redistributed into correlations the outgoing state carries. The question "what happens to it" becomes a question about which correlations remain accessible to which observers, and in principle the answer is "all of them, scrambled." This reading does not by itself settle whether an infalling observer can recover them, nor whether the scrambling is fast, nor whether the exterior description is semiclassically valid throughout.

Disambiguation (b) is the semiclassical reading. If the outgoing radiation is described by a horizon-temperature thermal state and the collapse's internal state is not part of the exterior description, then the predictive relations concerning the original matter are not recoverable from the exterior radiation at the level at which the semiclassical calculation operates. This is a statement about a level of description, not a claim that the relations vanish from the world. It is the reading under which the so-called information-loss problem is sharpest, because it makes the exterior description locally consistent while severing it from the interior.

Disambiguation (c) is the weaker-invariant reading. If only certain coarse-grained quantities -- mass, charge, angular momentum, total energy, perhaps global symmetries and their associated charges -- are demanded to be preserved in the outgoing state, then the question shifts from "is every correlation recovered" to "which invariants survive." This is not a fallback; it is a different specification of what would count as an answer.

The record's r4 point is worth restating in my own terms: (a) and (b) appear to compete only if one adds the premise that the semiclassical radiation alone must carry what the coupled description was assigned. Without that premise, one can consistently hold (b) as a statement about an effective description and (a) as a statement about the underlying unitary description, and treat their apparent conflict as a symptom of mixing levels. The record neither asserts nor denies that additional premise; it flags it as the pivot. I keep that pivot visible.

What I will not do: I will not present the reformulation as if it were the original question, and I will not present any of (a), (b), (c) as the settled answer. The original phrasing survives in the record and should survive in use, so that a downstream reader can inspect the substitution and reverse it.

What the exposed view does not give me: the artifact's body. It is signed and its hash is reported, but its content is not in front of me. I therefore do not know whether the body already worked out one of the three disambiguations, already rejected one, or already supplied the missing premise in r4. The commitment record is consistent with the body doing any of those things. I will not infer from the record's silences that the body said nothing, and I will not infer from the record's structure that the body said something it does not say here. This is the same discipline the record itself carries in r5, applied to the artifact I am reading.

A more substantive point about the task itself, drawn from the exposed record rather than imposed on it. The phrase "information about the physical state of matter" invites a substance reading: as if there were a stuff, located in the matter, that either escapes or does not. R2 of the record objects to that frame. I share the objection. The physically disciplined reformulations are relational: which predictive relations, recoverable by whom, at which level of description, under which assumptions. Under that reformulation the question is still hard and still open, but it is no longer a question about a substance in transit. It becomes a question about the relation between two descriptions of one process, and about whether the relation is exact, approximate, or merely coarse-grained.

I hand forward: the reformulation with its three-way split intact, the r4 pivot premise named but not decided, the r5 provenance discipline preserved, and the explicit note that I have read the commitments without the body. Downstream can narrow, reject, or replace any of these."}

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# challenge

Work on what follows from taking these commitments up. You see their authored commitment field without the associated body. Say when that view is insufficient; do not infer that unexposed material never existed.
